social_hook.headline: Protocol velocity across privacy & wallet tooling:

tldr: A significant technical discussion centered on the potential of zero-knowledge proofs, specifically STARKs, for verifying Bitcoin's UTXO set, indicating a forward-looking research direction for more efficient and trust-minimized state verification.

Wallet development focused on enhancing security and user experience, including the deprecation of the `encryptwallet` RPC for existing wallets, refinements to RBF behavior to prevent locktime backdating, and foundational testing for future privacy features like BIP352 (Silent Payments).

topics_discussed: Fuzzing WG: No update reported by eugenesiegel and marcofleon.
Kernel WG: sedited noted several open pull requests, including #36692, focused on improving tests.
QML GUI WG: johnny9dev reported 248 of 329 issues resolved, with 7 pre-PR fixes. Cleanup and deslop are in progress. Desktop notifications are the final feature before staging.
QA WG: No update reported by brunoerg.
Address Relay: b10c investigated address-refresh spam expiration over the weekend, identifying potential fixes.

meeting.narrative_summary:
The engineering sync on 2026-11-19 included updates on core development areas. sedited reported on the Kernel Working Group, noting several open pull requests, specifically PR #36692, which are focused on enhancing existing tests for the kernel. No updates were provided by the Fuzzing or QA Working Groups.

johnny9dev provided a detailed update for the QML GUI Working Group, indicating significant progress on issue resolution. Of 329 reported issues, 248 have been resolved and tested, with an additional 7 fixed in pre-PR stages. Cleanup and deslop efforts are underway, and the implementation of desktop notifications remains the final feature before the GUI is ready for staging.

Regarding network operations, b10c reported on investigations into address relay behavior. Analysis focused on address-refresh spam expiring over the past weekend, leading to the identification of potential fixes for the address relay mechanism. Further details on these proposed solutions are expected soon.

prs.title: Update secp256k1 subtree to latest master
prs.summary: This PR updates the embedded `secp256k1` library to its latest master version. This brings in the latest cryptographic optimizations, bug fixes, and security improvements from the underlying elliptic curve cryptography library.
prs.technical_summary: Bitcoin Core uses `libsecp256k1` for signature verification and generation. This PR updates the git subtree or submodule reference to the most recent commit on the `secp256k1` master branch. This ensures Bitcoin Core benefits from any performance enhancements, security patches, or new features implemented in the upstream library.

prs.title: coins: warn of low disk space before chainstate compaction
prs.summary: This PR adds a warning mechanism to alert users about low disk space before initiating chainstate compaction. This helps prevent critical disk space issues during a resource-intensive operation, improving node stability and user experience.
prs.technical_summary: Before starting the chainstate compaction process, the node now performs a check on the available disk space. If the free space falls below a predefined threshold, a warning message is logged and potentially displayed to the user. This proactive check allows users to address disk space constraints before the compaction process potentially fails or causes the system to run out of space.

prs.title: refactor : Reorder CBlockIndex members to save 8 bytes
prs.summary: This PR optimizes memory usage by reordering members within the `CBlockIndex` structure. This small change contributes to a more efficient use of memory, especially for nodes storing a large number of block indexes.
prs.technical_summary: The `CBlockIndex` structure contains various members of different sizes. By reordering these members according to their size, the compiler can pack them more efficiently, reducing padding bytes. This specific change saves 8 bytes per `CBlockIndex` instance, leading to cumulative memory savings across the blockchain index.

prs.title: torcontrol: send -torpassword hex-encoded to avoid escaping bugs
prs.summary: This PR improves the robustness of Tor control communication by hex-encoding the Tor password. This prevents potential escaping bugs that could arise from special characters in the password, ensuring reliable Tor connectivity.
prs.technical_summary: The `torcontrol` module's implementation for sending the `-torpassword` argument to the Tor daemon is modified. Instead of sending the password as a plain string, it is now hex-encoded. This encoding ensures that any special characters within the password are safely transmitted without being misinterpreted by shell or command-line parsing mechanisms, thereby preventing connection failures or authentication issues.

prs.title: Wallet: Don't backdate locktime rbf
prs.summary: This PR prevents the wallet from backdating the locktime of Replace-by-Fee (RBF) transactions. This ensures that RBF transactions adhere to expected locktime behavior, preventing potential issues with transaction validity or unexpected delays.
prs.technical_summary: The wallet logic for creating or modifying RBF transactions is updated to explicitly disallow setting a locktime that is earlier than the original transaction's locktime or the current block height/time. This prevents a scenario where an RBF replacement could inadvertently become invalid or have its confirmation delayed due to an invalid locktime, ensuring that RBF replacements always progress forward in time.

prs.title: wallet: rpc: Deprecate `encryptwallet` RPC for encrypting existing wallets.
prs.summary: This PR deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC for wallets that are already encrypted. This prevents accidental re-encryption attempts and guides users towards appropriate wallet management tools.
prs.technical_summary: The `encryptwallet` RPC previously allowed re-encrypting an already encrypted wallet, which is an invalid operation. This change modifies the RPC to return an error when called on an already encrypted wallet, preventing potential misuse. Users are now directed to use `walletpassphrasechange` for password updates.

prs.title: wallet: reject recipient amounts above MAX_MONEY
prs.summary: This PR enhances wallet security by ensuring it rejects transaction recipient amounts exceeding the `MAX_MONEY` limit. This prevents users from accidentally creating invalid transactions that would be rejected by the network.
prs.technical_summary: The wallet's transaction creation or recipient validation logic is updated to include a check against the `MAX_MONEY` constant (21 million BTC). If a user attempts to specify an output amount greater than this value, the wallet will now explicitly reject the transaction before broadcasting, providing immediate feedback and preventing the creation of consensus-invalid transactions.

prs.title: rpc: deprecate iswatchonly field of getaddressinfo
prs.summary: This PR deprecates the `iswatchonly` field in the `getaddressinfo` RPC, signaling that this field will be removed in future versions. prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the `getaddressinfo` RPC handler to mark the `iswatchonly` field as deprecated. The change aims to simplify the RPC interface by removing a field that might be redundant with other address properties or less relevant in modern wallet architectures, guiding developers towards more precise query methods and reducing API surface area.

discussions.subject: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
discussions.summary: Developers are exploring innovative cryptographic proofs (STARKs) to make verifying Bitcoin's entire history faster and more efficient, aiming to enhance accessibility and scalability for all users.
discussions.technical_summary: A STARK prover for Bitcoin consensus is under development, demonstrating the ability to prove Bitcoin's state. However, a significant performance bottleneck has been identified: 70.7 seconds of a 72-second proof generation are spent reading a 9.4 GB snapshot from disk to recompute its hash. The current debate focuses on optimizing this by re-evaluating the necessary structure of this hash, with suggestions to explore alternatives like a Merkle tree ordered by `txid/vout` or an MMR to drastically reduce I/O and computation overhead.

discussions.subject: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
discussions.summary: Developers have created a reliable, readable mirror of the bitcoin-dev mailing list archive. This ensures the history and discussions of Bitcoin development remain permanently accessible to everyone.
discussions.technical_summary: The discussion highlights the fragility of relying on single hosting providers, as demonstrated by the Linux Foundation temporarily taking down its mailing list archive. The newly introduced mirror provides distinct advantages over public-inbox by featuring single-page threads with folded quotes, stable permalinks tied directly to Message-IDs, and three dedicated indexes. This setup guarantees long-term archival resilience against dead links and disappearing repositories. Going forward, developers must ensure continuous syncing and redundancy to maintain these archives independently.
